metadata.case_name: Somaliland / Somalia (de facto fragmentation, inverted recognition)
metadata.author: V2 expansion (subagent draft)
metadata.key_test: Recognition-inverted de facto fragmentation: does FUNCTIONAL institutional capacity (Somaliland - unrecognized but governing) or FORMAL sovereignty (Somalia - recognized but collapsed) determine outcomes? The framework claims capacity. Tests complexity-control from the BOTTOM: Somaliland deliberately reduced complexity (smaller, more clan-homogeneous territory, distinct British-colonial legacy) to match limited capacity. Somaliland is an UNRECOGNIZED de facto state with NO separate WB data -> proxied via the parent reference + qualitative evidence (mirrors Aceh/Kosovo/East Timor sub-state handling).
metadata.notes: Reference-based record. Somalia (country_ref) carries real MI v1 re-scores - but they essentially measure Mogadishu/the recognized center, at the floor (P1 ~0.132). Somaliland (declared independence 1991; never internationally recognized) has no standalone WGI/WB coverage; its scores are intentionally null and its assessment is qualitative. Scored ~1996 vs 2024. The pre-event (1996) is already post-1991-split, so this is a comparative trajectory of the two de facto entities.

pre_event.event_description: By 1996, Somalia had collapsed into civil war and warlordism after the 1991 fall of Siad Barre; in the northwest, the former British Somaliland had declared independence (1991) and was building functional clan-negotiated institutions. The recognized state (Somalia) was failed; the unrecognized entity (Somaliland) was functional - an inversion of recognition and capacity.

context.fragmentation_mechanism: state collapse with de facto unrecognized secession (Somaliland)
context.growth_trajectory: collapse then partial, aided recovery off the floor

context.fragmentation_mechanism: de facto unrecognized secession + complexity-control from the bottom
context.backstop_details: Safeguard I in REVERSE: the ABSENCE of any great-power backstop championing recognition prevents formal statehood despite functional institutions - recognition, not capacity, is the binding constraint.
context.growth_trajectory: functional, clan-negotiated governance; modest growth (Berbera port/livestock)

a_trajectory_ranking.prediction: Somaliland (higher FUNCTIONAL capacity) > Somalia (recognized but floor-capacity). Capacity, not formal sovereignty, should predict the better outcome: Somaliland stabilizes and governs; Somalia remains failed (recovering only slowly off the floor).
a_trajectory_ranking.basis: Functional-P1 ordinality (Somaliland qualitatively well above Somalia's ~0.132 floor) + complexity-control from the bottom (Somaliland reduced territory/heterogeneity to match capacity).
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: Somalia (recognized) outperforms Somaliland, OR recognition status (not capacity) drives the outcome ranking.

b_violence.prediction: Somalia: critical violence RISK (floor-P1; al-Shabaab, warlordism). Somaliland: low-moderate RISK given functional capacity and clan power-sharing.
b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY
b_violence.falsification_condition: Somaliland descends into Somalia-level violence, or Somalia stabilizes to Somaliland's level.

c_convergence.prediction: Divergence: the recognized center and the unrecognized northwest diverge in governance and stability rather than re-converging into one functioning state.
c_convergence.basis: Capacity gap (functional Somaliland vs failed Somali center) widens; no re-integration.
c_convergence.falsification_condition: Convergence / re-integration into a single functioning state, or the capacity gap closing.

d_failure_dimension.prediction: Somalia fails on institutional capacity (P1) plus cohesion (P5). Somaliland's binding constraint is NOT capacity but the EXTERNAL recognition ceiling - a dimension the MI does not model.
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias.
d_failure_dimension.falsification_condition: Somaliland's constraint proves to be internal capacity failure rather than the external recognition ceiling.

e_fragment_count.prediction: 1 de facto successor (Somaliland), already split since 1991 but unrecognized; Safeguard B - Somalia's floor capacity cannot re-absorb or manage the fragment.
e_fragment_count.falsification_condition: Re-integration into a single recognized state, or further fragmentation of Somaliland itself.

f_reversal_risk.prediction: N/A - not a democratic-transition reversal case.

g_suppression_mechanism.classification: N/A - de facto fragmentation, not active suppression of Somaliland by the center (Mogadishu lacks the capacity to suppress).

h_substate_turbulence.prediction: Somaliland channels clan turbulence into negotiated power-sharing and elections (complexity-control from the bottom), staying functional despite non-recognition.
h_substate_turbulence.falsification_condition: Somaliland's internal turbulence escalates into Somalia-style collapse.

Somalia.outcome_summary: Recognized but failed, as predicted. Somalia remained at the institutional floor through 2024 - al-Shabaab insurgency, dependence on AU peacekeeping, fragile federal politics - though it recovered marginally off the absolute floor (P1 0.132 -> 0.173, MI 0.223 -> 0.245, Tier 4 throughout; P3 became scorable, P4 fell 0.357 -> 0.204). Formal sovereignty did not translate into functional outcomes.
key_events: fragile federal-member-state politics; recovery only marginally off the floor
2024 friction over the Somaliland-Ethiopia MoU (Berbera port access)

Somaliland.outcome_summary: [sub-state, unrecognized, no WB data] Qualitative: Somaliland sustained functional self-governance - multiple peaceful multiparty elections (incl. the 2024 presidential election with an incumbent conceding), functioning courts, clan power-sharing (the Guurti upper house), lower violence, and modest growth (Berbera port, livestock). Materially better governed than the recognized Somali center - yet still unrecognized internationally, the recognition ceiling the framework flags as an external (non-capacity) constraint.
key_events: sustained peaceful multiparty elections (incl. 2024 presidential transfer of power)
Berbera port development; 2024 Ethiopia MoU bid for sea access/recognition
still no international recognition despite functional statehood

analysis.overall_assessment: Strong confirmation of the capacity-over-sovereignty claim: 6/6 applicable predictions confirmed (d PARTIAL under the strict re-code). Functional capacity (Somaliland) predicted the better outcome despite the inversion of formal recognition.
safeguards_triggered: B (capacity gate: floor-capacity center cannot manage the fragment)
I in reverse (absence of a recognition backstop caps Somaliland's status)
H/complexity-control from the bottom (Somaliland reduced complexity to match capacity)
new_failure_modes_discovered: Recognition ceiling: an external (international-system) constraint that caps a functional entity's status independent of its institutional capacity - a dimension the MI does not model.
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Institutional capacity, not formal sovereignty, tracks outcomes: the unrecognized but functional entity (Somaliland) outperformed the recognized but collapsed state (Somalia) on every governance and stability measure. Somaliland achieved this by complexity-control from the BOTTOM - carving out a smaller, more clan-homogeneous, distinct-colonial-legacy entity matched to its capacity. The case also exposes a limit of the framework: a functional entity can be capped by an external recognition ceiling the MI does not capture.
proposed_framework_modifications: Flag a 'recognition ceiling' as an external constraint distinct from institutional capacity (candidate for the companion guide; needs the 50-case baseline check before any safeguard status).
analysis.baseline_impact: Candidate 'recognition ceiling' note needs the baseline check; otherwise additive (confirms capacity-over-sovereignty).
analysis.data_note: Somaliland is a non-WB unrecognized de facto entity; its scores are intentionally null and its assessment is qualitative. Somalia's WGI essentially measure the recognized center.
